unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision removes the entire night section, as did the first draft largely. It also strips the first draft's 'on the top floor with the legend painted across it "Esthonia Glassware Co."'. The telegram paragraph therefore runs straight into 'On the stroke of eleven' at 'the ground glass door', with no next-day marker and no named building or company.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Whittington set an eleven o'clock appointment at P9, and the later 'supper of buns the night before' (P56) implies the night passed.

evidence.quote: when Tuppence reached the block of buildings in which the offices of the Esthonia Glassware Co. were situated
On the stroke of eleven Tuppence came to a halt outside the ground glass door on the top floor with the legend painted across it
On the stroke of eleven Tuppence came to a halt outside the ground glass door. She knocked, and walked into a small rather dirty outer office.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'Next morning' and the first draft's 'on the top floor with the legend painted across it "Esthonia Glassware Co."'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: The night section is partly optional, but the 'Arrival at the office' section is planned; this is a residue of the authorized cuts.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Readers must infer that it is the following morning and that this is Whittington's office. The definite article has no antecedent.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Unmarked overnight jump and unanchored office door

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The clause 'She seized hurriedly on the first name that came into her head' is deleted. The archdeacon twinge now leads directly to 'Jane Finn' without stating that she is grabbing a random alias.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'she said hastily' and the archdeacon twinge still imply a false name. Chapter 002 retains 'fifth daughter of Archdeacon Cowley'.

evidence.quote: She seized hurriedly on the first name that came into her head.
She seized hurriedly on the first name that came into her head.
Tuppence's conscience gave her a passing twinge as she remembered the archdeacon.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the single sentence after the archdeacon twinge.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: the plan says she 'blurts "Jane Finn" to protect her father'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: This weakens the chance and coincidence mechanism and the motive of protecting her father. It also undercuts the truthfulness of her later 'hit upon it by chance', which Chapter IV builds on.
unresolved_should_improve.title: The improvised nature of 'Jane Finn' is cut

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts Tuppence's triumphant 'proved I have some wits to live by!' and Whittington's 'You can't play the innocent with me. You know a great deal more...'. As a result, 'I shouldn't like to contradict you' answers only 'perhaps it doesn't'. Her calculation about naming an impossible sum is also gone.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Blackmail, eh?', 'payment of services in advance' and V6 survive, so the scene's arc is intact.

evidence.quote: It seems to me that I have now proved I have some wits to live by!
You can’t play the innocent with me. You know a great deal more than you’re willing to admit.
You can't play the innocent with me. You know a great deal more than you're willing to admit.
you heard me say yesterday that I proposed to live by my wits. I admit I have knowledge of a certain name, but perhaps my knowledge ends there.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the 'proved I have some wits' sentence and Whittington's two-sentence 'play the innocent' rejoinder from the first draft.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: the plan calls for 'She plays the adventuress ("live by my wits")'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: 'Live by my wits' becomes a flat citation rather than a boast. The sly non-contradiction joke loses its target, which dulls Tuppence's adventuress performance.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Bluff escalation loses its comic turns

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Two lines are deleted: 'Knew all the time what I wanted you for, but kept up the comedy' and 'Thought you were quite a meek little kid with just enough brains for my purpose'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'like a cat and mouse' still conveys that he believes he has been played.

growled Whittington, with a sort of unwilling admiration. "All the same, some one's been talking.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore 'You took me in all right. Thought you were quite a meek little kid with just enough brains for my purpose.' and optionally the 'Knew all the time' sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: the plan specifies 'his grudging admiration' and 'believes she has been playing him'.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: These lines echo V2's 'sufficient intelligence... not to ask too many questions' and hint at a role without explaining it. They also pay off her 'small and demure' entrance. Without them, 'unwilling admiration' has no stated content.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Whittington's revealing admissions and the payoff of her meekness are cut

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Three beats are cut: 'Tuppence sped lightly down the stairs. A wild elation possessed her.' and Tommy's 'eyes opened to their fullest extent'. The scene now jumps from the office to 'A neighbouring clock' and to Tommy with no visible response to the cab.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: V8 survives, and Chapter 004 opens with the fare comedy.
